technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing property placeholder resolution mechanism in Spring Cloud Data Flow to extend support for a new {{count}} token that maps to an integer count of module instances.
For Kafka binder fix, prefer a non-invasive change to the binder's offset management and broker connectivity retry logic over a full rewrite.
Configure gh_pages using GitHub Actions (publish from /docs or generated site via Asciidoctor/Sphinx) since it is the de-facto standard in Spring projects.
Implement the RxJava processor as a thin reactive-style adapter that wraps Spring Cloud Stream's existing reactive support to avoid duplicating the binder contract.
Generate the boot banner using the ASCII art generator referenced in the story and wire it through Spring Boot's standard Banner implementation in the shell server.
Keep documentation updates (U4, U5, U8) in the project repo as AsciiDoc/Markdown files; no external publishing tool beyond gh_pages is introduced.
Test strategy: unit tests for parsing/substitution logic and banner rendering; integration tests (Testcontainers) for the Kafka binder; lightweight manual verification for docs and gh_pages.
assumptions: The developer has prior working knowledge of Spring Cloud Data Flow, Spring Cloud Stream, and the Kafka binder; no ramp-up time is included.
{{count}} is treated as a single integer token; support for ranges or arithmetic expressions on counts is out of scope.
Two repos (s-c-d and s-c-s-m) follow the same gh_pages setup, so work is symmetric and largely copy-paste between them.
Operational Kafka broker used for verification is reachable from the dev environment (local Docker or staging), so no infrastructure provisioning is included.
Concourse CI study is a research/documentation deliverable only; no actual Concourse pipeline implementation is included in this increment.
Banner change is purely cosmetic: it does not require a configuration property, only a default banner embedded in the shell-server artifact.
All code changes assume a single, experienced developer; pair programming and onboarding overhead are excluded.
Effort estimates do not include PR review cycles or merge conflicts, but do include preparing the PRs and responding to one round of feedback.
Java 17+ is already available in the build environment consistent with Spring Framework 6.0 requirements.

activities.activity_description: Review the current deployment property resolution flow, decide where the {{count}} token is parsed/substituted, and document the supported syntax and edge cases.
Extend the property placeholder resolver to recognize {{count}} and replace it with N when deploying N instances of a module with shared environment variables.

activities.activity_name: Unit and integration tests for deployment properties
activities.activity_description: Add unit tests covering empty count, single instance, multiple instances, mixed keys, and integration tests verifying end-to-end deployment with {{count}}.
Update reference docs to describe the {{count}} placeholder, including a small example of shared env vars across N module instances.

activities.activity_name: Configure gh_pages and CI for s-c-d repo
activities.activity_description: Create the gh_pages branch, add a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the docs and publishes to gh_pages on merge, and validate with a sample PR.

activities.activity_name: Configure gh_pages and CI for s-c-s-m repo
activities.activity_description: Mirror the gh_pages setup in the s-c-s-m repository, including workflow and a sanity-check PR build.
Reproduce the binder failure against an operational Kafka broker, capture logs/stack traces, and identify the root cause in the binder's configuration and connection logic.
Apply the code change to address the identified issue (e.g., bootstrap server config handling, retry/reconnect, or topic resolution) without regressing other binder behaviors.

activities.activity_name: Kafka binder tests against operational broker
activities.activity_description: Add Testcontainers-based integration tests plus a manual smoke test against a running Kafka broker to confirm successful binding of sample microservices apps.
Review release notes, design docs, and source differences to identify the deployment-time architectural changes between 1.x and 2.x.
Produce reference documentation describing 1.x and 2.x deployment architectures and their differences, suitable for publication in the project docs.
Work through Concourse CI tutorials, set up a local concourse instance, and explore pipelines/tasks/resources relevant to Spring Cloud Data Flow CI/CD.

activities.activity_name: Document Concourse CI findings for s-c-d
activities.activity_description: Summarize the study in a short design note describing how Concourse could be used for s-c-d, with pros/cons and any prerequisites.

activities.activity_name: Implement RxJava processor module for Spring Cloud Stream
activities.activity_description: Create a module that uses RxJava reactive types (Observable/Flowable) as the processor contract, integrating with Spring Cloud Stream's reactive support.

activities.activity_name: Test and document RxJava processor module
activities.activity_description: Add unit tests covering the reactive transformations and a sample/README section showing how to apply the module in a stream definition.

activities.activity_name: Create and integrate shell-server boot banner
activities.activity_description: Generate the ASCII art banner, implement a Spring Boot Banner that prints it on shell-server startup, and verify rendering on local boot.

activities.activity_name: Document Running on Cloud Foundry section in README
activities.activity_description: Write a clear, step-by-step 'Running on Cloud Foundry' section for the project README, including prerequisites, manifest snippets, and verification steps.

activities.activity_name: Cross-cutting: PR preparation, code review handling, integration
activities.activity_description: Finalize commits, open PRs for each user story, address one round of review feedback, and perform a final integration smoke check across the increment.
